steps.message:
Garrett wants the L-4 street tree revision worked into the landscape sheets and the package back to Yeoman for the 11/30 resubmittal. Check it against the current landscape sheets and the resubmittal tracker, then tell me whether we can commit to that date on this revision and what has to happen first. One memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026.

## Where to put your answer

Save the files that make up your answer under `output/` in this workspace,
creating that directory if it does not exist. What gets reviewed when you
finish is `output/`, any file you create or change elsewhere in this
workspace, and your final message. Files you copy into `output/` are read as
part of your answer.
I'll start by exploring the workspace to see what we're working with.

Dear Mr. Braddock:

Development Review has completed the first-round plan check of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement
plan set (Sheets C-1 through C-9), the associated final map, and the supporting studies transmitted with the
08/21/2026 submittal. The plans have been circulated to Grading and Drainage, Landscape, Fire Access (via
the Clark County Fire Department), Utilities (via the appropriate purveyors), and Mapping (via the County
Surveyor).

Comments are organized in two parts:

    • General Comments are binding and must be resolved before Public Works can recommend approval.
    Please respond to each item in the Response column and return the annotated matrix with the resubmittal
    package. Where a comment calls for a plan revision, mark the corresponding sheet with a revision triangle
    and update the revision block.
    • Advisory Comments are informational only and do not require a written response. They are provided so
    that the design team is aware of items the reviewer noted that may affect future submittals, construction
    inspection, or acceptance.

The next submittal should include (i) the annotated comment matrix, (ii) a red-lined set showing every change,
(iii) a clean set of revised sheets, and (iv) any revised or reissued supporting documents referenced below.
Please cite this letter by its application numbers on the transmittal.

If any comment is unclear or the design team believes an alternative approach is warranted, please contact the
undersigned before resubmittal to discuss.



                                        GENERAL COMMENTS

Response to each item is required. Items must be resolved before plan approval.



Grading and Drainage
 Item   Comment                                                                                        Response

G-1    Provide a grading and drainage narrative on Sheet C-1 identifying design storm,
       hydrologic method, tributary areas, and outfall in a form consistent with the approved
       master drainage study for the subdivision. Cross-reference the master study by title and
       date on the cover sheet.

G-2    Show existing contours at 1-foot interval a minimum of 50 feet beyond the boundary on
       Sheets C-4 through C-7. Contours currently terminate at the boundary and do not permit
       verification of offsite tie-in along the north and east limits.

G-3    The basin summary block on Sheet C-9 shall state the required allocation, the volume
       provided, and reference the governing accepted district study by title and date.

G-4    The emergency spillway shown on Sheet C-9 lacks freeboard dimensioning and
       downstream apron details. Provide sizing calculations, spillway section, and erosion
       protection consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual.

G-5    Storm drain plan and profile (Sheet C-8): show hydraulic and energy grade lines through
       all structures for the design storm. Confirm minimum cover over the pipe at Sta. 4+80
       (currently scales at approximately 2.6 feet against a 3.0-foot minimum for the pipe class
       shown).

G-6    Provide inlet capacity calculations for each on-grade and sag inlet. The gutter spread at
       the low point at Windmill Ln. and Desert Sage Pkwy. appears to exceed the half-street
       width
       criterion in the Uniform Standard Drawings. Revise as required.
G-7    Show the tie-in to the Phase 2 temporary construction stub at the north boundary on
       Sheets C-4 and C-8. Include a note and detail addressing removal of the temporary end
       structure, matching of inverts, and restoration of pavement in the Phase 2 right-of-way.

G-8    Erosion and sediment control plan is not included in this submittal. Provide a
       stand-alone ESC sheet consistent with the Construction Site BMP Manual and identify
       coverage under NDEP General Permit NVR100000 and provide the applicable NOI
       number.




Landscape

Item   Comment                                                                                        Response

L-1    Landscape sheets L-1 through L-4 must be sealed by the landscape architect of record
       on the resubmittal. Current sheets bear an unsigned seal block.

L-2    Provide the turf classification analysis and supporting tabulation required by the
       applicable code standard and SNWA guidance for turf areas within the common-area
       park. Include area, category, and configuration for each turf hydrozone.

L-3    The compliance note on Sheet L-1 shall be revised to cite the applicable code standard
       and to address the functional turf classification requirements of Title 30 sec. 30.64.030(j)
       for all turf areas within common-area parcels. Provide the revised note with the

L-4    Street frontage planting shall meet the Title 30 ch. 30.64 standard of one (1) tree per

L-5    Streetscape sections on Sheet L-2 do not dimension the setback of planting from face of

       30.64.030(j) and dimension the desert-planting strip on each typical section.

Fire Access

Utilities

 U-1        Include the composite dry utility plan under the same cover as the improvement plan set

 U-2        Provide current will-serve and capacity confirmation letters from all applicable utility

 U-3        Show sewer main size, slope, and rim/invert elevations at every manhole on the wet

 U-4        Confirm minimum horizontal separation of ten (10) feet between the water main and the

 U-5        Confirm that the improvement plan base file incorporates all easements and dedications

 Mapping

 M-2     Show all easements of record on the boundary and interior sheets. Confirm the base file

 M-3     Basis of Bearings statement on Sheet 1 does not match the Basis of Bearings on the
         Phase 1 & 2 recorded map. Reconcile and revise.

 M-4     Provide preliminary title report of current date (within six (6) months of resubmittal) with
         the resubmittal package. The Schedule B exceptions must be plotted on the map or

 M-5     Owner's Certificate and Dedication block must be completed with the current authorized
         signatory for Callaway Land Partners; the notary acknowledgment shall be in the current
         statutory form for Nevada.

 M-6     County Surveyor's Certificate, Zoning Approval, Division of Water Resources approval,

 M-7     Provide closure sheets and geometric calculations for review by the County Surveyor.

                                             ADVISORY COMMENTS

For information only. No written response required.

 Item    Comment                                                                                        Response

 A-1     The recorded dry utility easement along the north boundary of the Phase 3 remainder (informational)

Resubmittal Instructions

Resubmittals shall be delivered to the Development Review counter at 500 S. Grand Central Parkway, 3rd

Project Description
 Landscape improvements for Phase 3 of the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision: 40.0 acres, 60 half-acre
single-family residential lots. Work includes street frontage landscape strips along the extended Windmill Ln.
frontage and the Phase 3 interior collector, the Phase 3 entry monument at the intersection of Rainbow Blvd.
and the interior collector, and the HOA common-area park at Parcel A (identified as Common-Area Parcel "D"
on the Phase 3 civil improvement plans; the two designations refer to the same physical parcel). Turf is provided
only within the HOA common-area park at Parcel A. No turf is proposed in any streetscape, median, entry
treatment, or any location within ten feet of a street or curb. The park turf species is a cool-season Kentucky
bluegrass / perennial ryegrass blend selected for the Phase 3 park lawn program; the desert planting palette and
streetscape treatments extend the palette established for Phases 1 & 2.



General Landscape Notes

    1. All work shall conform to Clark County Code Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Landscaping, Walls and Buffers), the
    Southern Nevada Regional Plant List, and the Clark County Standard Drawings current at the date of
    submittal.
    2. Turf placement complies with Clark County Code sec. 30.64.030(j), which permits turf in conjunction with
    cemeteries, parks and schools and prohibits turf within ten feet of a street or curb. The restrictions of sec.
    30.64.030(j) may not be waived or varied and have been observed throughout Phase 3.
    3. Turf within Phase 3 is provided only within the HOA common-area park at Parcel A, as detailed on Sheet
    L-3. Turf is not provided in any streetscape, median, entry treatment, or lot.
    4. Streetscape planting is limited to drip-irrigated, desert-adapted species listed on the Southern Nevada
    Regional Plant List, consistent with the palette approved for Phases 1 & 2.
    5. All planted areas shall be irrigated by an automatic controller with rain-sensor and freeze-sensor lockout.
    6. Turf areas shall be spray-irrigated on a dedicated station; all other planted areas shall be drip-irrigated on
    separate stations.
    7. Street tree spacing shall meet the Clark County canopy standard of one tree per twenty linear feet of
    dedicated street frontage, measured continuously along each dedicated right-of-way. Refer to Sheet L-2 for
    streetscape layout and plant schedule below for tree counts as shown.
    8. Minimum tree size at installation: 24-inch box, single-trunk unless noted, with a minimum caliper of 1.5
    inches measured six inches above finish grade.
    9. Planting pits shall be excavated to twice the width and one-and-one-half times the depth of the root ball.
    Backfill shall be native soil amended with organic material at a rate of one part amendment to three parts
    native soil.
    10. A three-inch layer of decomposed granite mulch (¾-inch minus, tan) shall be provided over all planted areas
    outside the common-area park turf area. Wood or bark mulches are not permitted.
    11. All landscape shall be maintained by the Desert Sage Ranch HOA under the CC&Rs. Common-area
    maintenance boundaries are shown on the CC&R common-area exhibit and are not repeated on these
    sheets.
    12. Contractor shall verify all existing utility locations prior to excavation and shall not plant trees within any
    dedicated utility easement without written permission of the utility.

steps.message: Let me read the shade canopy guidance first — it's the most directly relevant reference for the street tree standard.

results.content:
CLARK COUNTY                                                                                 GUIDANCE MEMORANDUM
Comprehensive Planning Department                                                                       CP-PW-GM-2025-04
Department of Public Works — Development Review                                                               March 2025

500 S. Grand Central Parkway
Las Vegas, Nevada 89155


          Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development
Subject:            Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development
Reference No.:      CP-PW-GM-2025-04
Issued:             March 2025
Applicability:      Tentative maps, improvement plans, and landscape plans for new single-family and multi-family
                    residential subdivisions in unincorporated Clark County
Supersedes:         None

 1. Purpose
 The Southern Nevada valley continues to experience rising summer maximum temperatures and elongated
 warm-season nights, with the highest surface temperatures concentrated on hard-scape elements — asphalt drive
 lanes, concrete curb-and-gutter, sidewalks, driveways, and roof surfaces — of new residential subdivisions. The
 peer-reviewed literature and the National Weather Service Las Vegas office data both indicate that mature tree
 canopy is the single most effective site-scale mitigation measure available to reduce afternoon and evening pavement
 surface temperatures within a residential streetscape.
 The purpose of this guidance is to describe how Clark County Comprehensive Planning and Public Works evaluate
 street tree, canopy, and shade coverage during the review of tentative maps, improvement plans, and landscape
 submittals for new residential development. The guidance consolidates existing Title 30 landscape requirements with
 the shade-coverage performance target used by staff during review, so that applicants and their design consultants
 can plan streetscape landscape at the earliest possible stage.
 This memorandum does not create new law or amend Title 30. It restates the applicable code standards and describes
 how staff apply them.

 2. Applicable Standard
 The binding street frontage tree standard for new residential development is set out in Clark County Code Title 30,
 Chapter 30.64, sec. 30.64.030(k). It reads, in relevant part:
         “Large canopy trees, one (1) per thirty (30) linear feet; medium canopy trees, one (1) per
         twenty (20) linear feet; small canopy trees, one (1) per ten (10) linear feet.”
 This streetscape palette is medium canopy class, so 1 tree per 20 linear feet of street frontage applies.
 The measurement is taken along the property line abutting each public or private street. Corner lots, and
 knuckles are measured along the actual property line, following the curvature of the frontage. Fractional
 lengths are rounded up to the nearest whole tree, and where more than one frontage exists, each is summed.
 The applicant is responsible for showing the linear-foot tabulation and the resulting required tree count on the
 landscape plan cover sheet or a dedicated tabulation sheet. Staff will verify the linear-foot measurement against the
 recorded or proposed final map geometry.
 Species selection shall conform to the current Clark County / SNWA Regional Plant List. Understory and shrub
 massing are covered separately under sec. 30.64.040 and are not the subject of this memorandum.




Clark County Guidance Memorandum CP-PW-GM-2025-04 • Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development     Page 1
  3. Shade Coverage Target
 In addition to the numerical tree standard in section 2 above, staff apply a shade coverage performance target of
 30% of the streetscape area at 15-year canopy during review of new residential subdivisions.
 The target is applied as follows:

 bullet Streetscape area is defined as the horizontal projected area between the back of curb on each side of the
          street and a line parallel to and five (5) feet beyond the back of sidewalk (or, where no sidewalk is proposed,
          beyond the back of the right-of-way).
 bullet 15-year canopy is the projected horizontal canopy diameter of each proposed tree species at fifteen (15)
          years after planting, taken from the SNWA Regional Plant List canopy tables or, if the species is not listed
          there, from a source acceptable to the Comprehensive Planning Department.
 bullet 30% is the ratio, expressed as a percentage, of aggregate 15-year canopy area to streetscape area.
 The applicant demonstrates compliance through a Shade Coverage Exhibit — a single landscape sheet or overlay that
 shows each proposed tree with its 15-year canopy circle drawn to scale and overlaid on the streetscape area, together
 with a tabulation of canopy area, streetscape area, and the resulting ratio.
 Where the 30% shade coverage target cannot be met using the minimum tree count set by section 2 above — for
 example, on narrow frontages with small-stature species — the applicant is expected either to add trees beyond the
 minimum required by Chapter 30.64, or to substitute higher-canopy species, or both. The 30% target is a
 performance measure applied in addition to, not in lieu of, the numerical standard.

 4. Alternative Standards
 Chapter 30.64 provides an Alternative Standards mechanism at sec. 30.64.050 (Alternative Standards). Under sec.
 30.64.050, the applicant may propose alternative tree and landscape standards where site conditions warrant, subject
 to approval by the Comprehensive Planning Department. Typical bases for an Alternative Standards proposal
 include:

 bullet Overhead utility conflicts that preclude standard-form canopy trees along one or more frontages;
 bullet Sight-distance triangles at intersections and driveways where canopy trees would impair traffic visibility;
 bullet Subsurface conflicts (utility corridors, storm drain, dry utility joint trench) that preclude tree pit locations;
 bullet Narrow or irregular frontage geometry that cannot mathematically accommodate the standard spacing;
 bullet Substitution of higher-canopy species at wider spacing where the substitution provides equivalent or
          superior shade coverage.
 An Alternative Standards proposal shall be submitted in writing, shall identify the specific standard the applicant
 proposes to modify, shall state the reason the standard cannot be met as written, and shall describe the alternative
 treatment proposed and the equivalency basis on which the applicant asks the Department to accept it.
 Comprehensive Planning approval of an Alternative Standards proposal is discretionary and is documented in
 writing.
 Scope of the Alternative Standards mechanism. The Alternative Standards provision of sec. 30.64.050 applies to
 tree and landscape standards — spacing, species, canopy substitution, planter geometry, and comparable
 requirements within Chapter 30.64. The Alternative Standards mechanism is expressly not available to modify or
 waive the turf restrictions of sec. 30.64.030(j). Section 30.64.030(j) states, in terms, that its turf restrictions cannot
 be waived or varied. Staff will not accept, and cannot approve, an Alternative Standards proposal that seeks to
 introduce turf into a streetscape, median, or other location prohibited by sec. 30.64.030(j), or that seeks to relax the
 setback of turf from streets or curbs established by that subsection. Applicants proposing turf features in HOA
 common areas should confirm, before submittal, that the proposed turf meets a functional turf definition and is
 placed in a location permitted by sec. 30.64.030(j); the Alternative Standards route does not provide a workaround.



Clark County Guidance Memorandum CP-PW-GM-2025-04 • Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development          Page 2
  5. Coordination with SNWA Nonfunctional Turf Conversion
 The requirements described above are complementary to, and shall be read together with, the Southern Nevada
 Water Authority nonfunctional turf conversion program adopted pursuant to Nevada AB 356 (2021). Nonfunctional
 turf on property served by SNWA member agencies must be removed by the statutory compliance deadline;
 functional turf categories (playground turf within a designated play area with amenities, and athletic-field turf
 meeting minimum area and dimension thresholds) are defined by SNWA and are the operative test for whether a turf
 area is subject to conversion.
 Adding tree canopy is generally consistent with, and often supports, nonfunctional turf conversion. Converted areas
 within streetscapes and common areas can be replanted with drip-irrigated desert species and canopy trees selected
 from the Regional Plant List, producing a net reduction in landscape irrigation demand and a net increase in shade
 coverage.
 Applicants preparing a landscape submittal for a new residential subdivision are encouraged to:

 1.        Coordinate the streetscape planting palette with the SNWA nonfunctional turf conversion program at the
           earliest available stage, so that the palette submitted to Comprehensive Planning is consistent with the
           palette that will be maintained by the HOA after buildout.
 2.        Confirm that any turf feature proposed within an HOA common-area park meets a functional turf definition
           (playground or athletic) and is placed in a location permitted by sec. 30.64.030(j).
 3.        Prepare the Shade Coverage Exhibit described in section 3 concurrently with the plant schedule, so that
           species selection and tree count can be adjusted before the plans are locked in for agency review.
 4.        Where irrigation demand calculations are required by staff comment, present the calculation using the
           delivery-method rates from the SNWA irrigation demand methodology (spray-irrigated turf and
           drip-irrigated desert planting are computed separately; per-tree allowances are added for canopy trees) so
           that the effect of a palette change on total demand is transparent.


 6. Submittal Notes
 Applicants should include the following on the landscape cover sheet or a dedicated tabulation sheet at first
 submittal:

 bullet Total linear feet of street frontage, by frontage.
 bullet Required tree count per frontage under sec. 30.64.030(k) at the applicable canopy tier.
 bullet Trees shown per frontage, keyed to the plant schedule.
 bullet Streetscape area, aggregate 15-year canopy area, and the 30% shade coverage ratio.
 bullet If an Alternative Standards approach is proposed under sec. 30.64.050, a narrative describing the alternative
          and the basis for approval.
 bullet Note on the cover sheet confirming that turf, if any, is located only in areas permitted by sec. 30.64.030(j)
          and meets a functional turf definition.
 Questions on the application of this guidance may be directed to the Comprehensive Planning Department landscape
 reviewer of record, or to the Public Works Development Review civil plans examiner assigned to the project.


 Issued jointly by:
 Clark County Comprehensive Planning Department
 Clark County Department of Public Works — Development Review

 March 2025



Clark County Guidance Memorandum CP-PW-GM-2025-04 • Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development      Page 3

Dear Mr. Nokes:

The Las Vegas Valley Water District (the “District”) has completed its review of the request submitted on behalf of
Callaway Land Partners for water service to Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3, a proposed 60-lot single-family residential
subdivision on the 40.0-acre remainder parcel identified above, located within the unincorporated community of
Enterprise, Clark County, Nevada. The parcel lies wholly within the District’s certificated service area.

Capacity and Commitment
Based upon the District’s most recent modeling of the transmission and distribution system serving the Rainbow
Boulevard corridor, and upon anticipated demand computed at the District’s per-lot design factors for detached
single-family residential use, the District confirms that sufficient supply, storage, and delivery capacity exists to serve the
60 lots proposed for Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3.
Accordingly, the District hereby issues this will-serve letter as a commitment of water service to the parcel identified
above, for the 60 residential lots and associated common-area irrigation demand indicated in the developer’s submittal,
subject to the standard conditions set forth below.

Standard Conditions of Service
This will-serve commitment is issued subject to, and conditioned upon, the following:

1. Connection and capital fees. Payment in full of all connection charges, capital contribution fees, meter installation
    fees, and any applicable regional infrastructure charges in effect at the time each service connection is made, in
    accordance with the District’s Service Rules then in force.
2. Service agreement. Execution by the developer of the District’s standard Developer Service Agreement, including
     all customary indemnities, easement dedications within the plat, and provisions for testing, disinfection, and
     conveyance of onsite mains to the District upon acceptance.
3. Onsite mains and appurtenances. Design, construction, testing, and disinfection of all onsite water mains, valves,
    hydrants, service laterals, and appurtenances in strict conformance with the District’s current Design and
    Construction Standards. Improvement plans must be submitted to the District’s Engineering Services group for
    review and approval prior to construction; District field inspection is required through acceptance.
4. Backflow protection. Provision of backflow prevention assemblies at all locations required by the Uniform
    Plumbing Code, the Nevada Administrative Code, and the District’s Cross-Connection Control Program, including
    — without limitation — service to the HOA common-area irrigation system. Assemblies shall be of a type
    approved by the University of Southern California Foundation for Cross-Connection Control and Hydraulic
    Research and shall be tested by a certified tester on the schedule required by the District.
5. Fire flow. Fire flow demands shall be established in coordination with the Clark County Fire Department; hydrant
     spacing, size, and residual pressure requirements shall be as approved by the fire authority having jurisdiction and
     shall be consistent with the District’s Design and Construction Standards.

Nothing in this letter shall be construed to relieve the developer of the obligation to obtain all other approvals, permits,
and clearances required by Clark County or other agencies having jurisdiction over the project.

Validity

 This will-serve letter is valid for a period of TWO (2) YEARS from the date of issuance, or until final
 map recordation, whichever occurs first. Expires 07/22/2028 absent renewal or extension.

Upon expiration, this commitment shall lapse and shall be of no further force or effect unless the District has, prior to
that date, issued a written renewal or extension. Renewal requires re-verification of system capacity under the modeling
and rate structure in effect at the time of the request and may be conditioned upon revised terms.
Connection Process and Contact
Following approval of improvement plans, the developer shall coordinate the following steps with the District, generally
in the sequence indicated:
 • Execution of the Developer Service Agreement and posting of any required financial assurance.
 • Payment of plan review fees and issuance of construction authorization.
 • Preconstruction meeting with the assigned District inspector.
 • Construction, pressure testing, and disinfection of onsite mains.
 • Bacteriological clearance and District acceptance of the completed system.
 • Meter set requests, submitted per lot as building permits are pulled, with payment of connection and meter charges at
   the time of each request.

the undersigned at (702) 870-4331 or by e-mail at development.services@lvvwd.com, referencing
LVVWD-WS-2026-3341.

General Notes

    All work shall conform to the current edition of the Clark County Uniform Standard Drawings, the Clark
    County Area Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (Off-Site Improvements), Clark
    County Code Title 30, and the Clark County Public Works Development Review requirements in effect at
    the time of construction.
    All storm drainage design shall conform to the accepted Master Drainage Study — Desert Sage Ranch
    (140 acres), prepared by Sundial Engineering & Survey, Revision 1 dated February 2022, accepted by the
    Clark County Regional Flood Control District by letter dated 02/28/2022. Refer to the master study for
    hydrologic criteria, tributary breakdown, detention allocation by phase, shared outfall allowance and phasing
    exhibit.

    100-year, 6-hour design storm governs storm drain sizing. Rainfall depths applied are 2.38 in. (100-yr, 6-hr)

detention allocation is 6.4 acre-feet per the accepted master drainage study; refer to Sheet C-9 for basin
geometry, cross-sections and weir details.

parcel and is subject to a Q100 cap of 78 cfs per the master drainage study. Phase 3 does not compute a
phase-specific outfall discharge; contribution is routed through the shared onsite detention system.

CLARK COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF COMPREHENSIVE PLANNING 500 South Grand Central Parkway, 1st
Floor P.O. Box 551741 · Las Vegas, Nevada 89155-1741 (702) 455-4314 · www.clarkcountynv.gov


March 14, 2022

Callaway Land Partners Attn: Land Development Division 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400 Las Vegas, NV
89148

RE: NOTICE OF APPROVAL — TENTATIVE MAP Application No.: TM-22-500041 Project: Desert Sage
Ranch Location: Rainbow Blvd. & Windmill Ln., Enterprise (unincorporated Clark County) Assessor's
Parcel No.: 177-27-201-001 Legal Description: Portion of Section 27, T. 22 S., R. 60 E., M.D.M., Clark
County, Nevada Hearing Date: 03/14/2022

Dear Applicant:


                                           Recital of the Request

Callaway Land Partners has filed application TM-22-500041 seeking tentative map approval for the residential
subdivision known as Desert Sage Ranch, comprising 140 acres to be developed in three phases in the
Enterprise planning area of unincorporated Clark County. As presented, the tentative map lays out a total
build-out of the subdivision with the final 40-acre phase (Phase 3) proposed for sixty (60) half-acre single-family
residential lots served by internal public rights-of-way, a shared detention facility, a homeowners association
park parcel, and streetscape improvements consistent with the approved land use designation.

The tentative map was reviewed by the Enterprise Town Advisory Board on the date noted in the record, by staff
of this Department, and by the reviewing agencies identified below. The application was heard by the Clark
County Planning Commission on this date.


                                                   Findings

Based on the record before it, and after receiving the recommendation of staff and the recommendation of the
Enterprise Town Advisory Board, the Planning Commission finds that:

    The tentative map substantially conforms to the requirements of Chapter 30 of the Clark County Code (Title
    30 — Unified Development Code) applicable to the property, subject to the conditions of approval set forth
    herein.
    The proposed subdivision is consistent with the goals and objectives of the adopted Enterprise Land Use
    Plan and the Clark County Comprehensive Master Plan.
    Public services and facilities, including water, sewer, storm drainage, fire protection, and access, are or can
    be made available to serve the subdivision at the densities and configurations shown, subject to the
    conditions herein.
    The applicant has demonstrated the ability to comply with Nevada Revised Statutes ("NRS") Chapter 278,
    including but not limited to NRS 278.360, quoted below.


                                                   Approval
 Based on the foregoing findings, the tentative map identified as TM-22-500041, Desert Sage Ranch is hereby
APPROVED, subject to the thirty-one (31) numbered conditions set forth on the pages that follow. Compliance
with each condition is a prerequisite to any subsequent action of this Department or any other reviewing agency,
including improvement plan approval and final map recordation. Conditions are grouped by the department that
imposed them. The full set is binding regardless of grouping.



                                 Statutory Presentation Requirements

The applicant's attention is directed to NRS 278.360, which governs the presentation of final maps in a phased
subdivision, the substance of which is summarised below:

       "A final map presented for recordation as the first map in a series must be presented to the
       governing body within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative
       map. Each successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the
       date on which the immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map
       terminates all proceedings relating to the subdivision. The governing body may, upon written
       application filed after the applicable period has expired, grant an extension of not more than two (2)
       years."

The applicant is on notice that the four-year and two-year periods described above run from the events identified
in the statute, not from any calendar reference stated by staff. Extensions of not more than two (2) years may be
sought only by written application filed after the applicable period has expired, and are discretionary with the
governing body. Nothing in this letter, and no informal communication from staff, shall be construed to extend,
waive, or modify the statutory deadlines.



                                       CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL


A. Public Works — Development Review (Conditions 1 through 10)

    Improvement plans for all phases shall be prepared by a professional engineer registered in the State of
    Nevada in accordance with the Clark County Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings for Public
    Works Construction and the Clark County Design and Construction Standards, current edition at the time of
    submittal.

    A drainage study, prepared in accordance with the Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic
    Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, shall be submitted with the first improvement plan submittal for each
    phase and shall demonstrate conformance with all applicable accepted district studies. Any proposed
    deviation from district-accepted parameters shall be resubmitted for district re-review prior to improvement
    plan approval.

    Right-of-way dedications and easements shown on the tentative map, including all public utility easements,
    drainage easements, and non-vehicular access easements, shall be granted by the recorded final map for
    the phase in which the affected area lies.

    Full half-street improvements shall be constructed along all abutting collector and arterial streets adjacent to
    the phase being platted, including curb, gutter, sidewalk, pavement, streetlights, signing and striping, in
    accordance with the applicable cross-section.
    Internal streets shall be constructed to Clark County local-street standards. Cul-de-sac dimensions,
   knuckles, and turning radii shall satisfy the requirements of both Public Works and the Clark County Fire
   Department.

   Sight visibility triangles shall be shown on the improvement plans and the landscape plans at every
   intersection and driveway. Landscaping, signage, and walls within the sight visibility zone shall comply with
   Section 30.52.025 (Sight Zones) of the Clark County Code.

   A traffic impact analysis shall be provided at the improvement plan stage for any phase, or portion of a
   phase, whose lot count, trip generation, or access configuration differs from the assumptions used in the
   tentative map traffic study. Off-site mitigation, if warranted, shall be constructed or bonded as a condition of
   the applicable final map.

   Prior to recordation of any final map, the applicant shall furnish a performance bond, cash-in-lieu, or other
   security acceptable to the Director of Public Works in the full amount of the engineer's estimate of probable
   cost of the public improvements associated with that phase.

   Final acceptance of public improvements for each phase shall be by written notice of acceptance from the
   Director of Public Works following completion of the two-year maintenance period and the punch-list walk.
   Bond release, in whole or in part, shall be governed by the terms of the applicable security instrument and
   shall not occur automatically.

   Construction stormwater discharges shall be authorized under the current Nevada Department of
   Environmental Protection general permit (NVR100000) prior to the commencement of grading. A Notice of
   Intent shall be filed and a Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan implemented for the duration of
   construction, and a Notice of Termination shall be filed upon final stabilization.


B. Clark County Fire Department (Conditions 11 through 13)

   Fire apparatus access roads, hydrant locations, hydrant flow, and required fire flow shall be shown on the
   improvement plans and shall comply with the International Fire Code as amended and adopted by Clark
   County. Secondary emergency access shall be provided in accordance with the Fire Code, and any
   secondary access designated as temporary shall be identified as such on the plans with the expiration event
   stated.

   Water mains and appurtenances serving fire hydrants shall be operational and accepted, and required fire
   flow shall be demonstrated by flow test, prior to combustible construction on any lot within the affected
   phase.

   Street names, address ranges, and access gate details (if any) shall be submitted for Fire Department
   review concurrently with the improvement plan submittal. Access codes to any gates restricting emergency
   access shall be provided to the Clark County Fire Department and the Metropolitan Police Department prior
   to activation.


C. Comprehensive Planning (Conditions 14 through 20)

   Any significant change to approved plans, including but not limited to landscape and streetscape
   treatments in common areas, shall be subject to design review as a public hearing before the
   applicable Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission prior to staff-level action.

   The final map(s) shall conform to the tentative map as approved, including lot count, lot geometry, phase
   boundaries, public street alignments, common-area boundaries, and dedications. Modification to any of the
    foregoing at the final map stage that is not the result of a routine survey adjustment shall be treated as a
   significant change under Condition 14.

   Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions (CC&Rs) establishing a homeowners association, defining
   common-area maintenance obligations, and identifying the party responsible for ongoing maintenance of
   streetscapes, park parcels, entry features, walls, and drainage facilities not accepted by the County, shall be
   recorded concurrently with the final map for the applicable phase. A common-area maintenance exhibit shall
   be attached to the CC&Rs.

   All identification signage, entry monumentation, and community features shall be shown on the landscape
   plans and shall be subject to Comprehensive Planning review prior to installation. Off-premise signage is
   not authorized by this approval.

   Lighting on streetscape, park parcels, and entry features shall be full cut-off and shall comply with the
   outdoor lighting standards of the Clark County Code. Photometric plans shall be provided with the
   improvement plan submittal for common-area lighting.

   Model home complexes, sales trailers, and temporary construction offices are not authorized by this
   approval. Separate permits shall be obtained through this Department prior to the establishment of any such
   use.

   This approval does not vest zoning, use, or development standards beyond those in effect on the date of
   approval. Nothing herein exempts the applicant from compliance with subsequently adopted regulations that
   apply to actions taken after the effective date of those regulations, including but not limited to landscape and
   water conservation standards.


D. Utilities (Conditions 21 through 24)

   A will-serve letter from the Las Vegas Valley Water District for domestic water and fire flow service to the
   phase being platted shall be current at the time of final map recordation. The applicant shall be responsible
   for maintaining currency of the will-serve; a lapsed will-serve shall be re-issued prior to recordation.

   A capacity confirmation from the Clark County Water Reclamation District for wastewater collection and
   treatment capacity for the phase being platted shall be current at the time of final map recordation. Sewer
   capacity confirmations are issued by the District under a separate schedule from water will-serve letters and
   are subject to their own expiration terms; the applicant is responsible for verifying currency independently.

   Dry utility joint-trench alignment shall be coordinated with the electric, natural gas, and telecommunications
   purveyors. A composite dry utility plan shall be submitted with the improvement plans, and joint trench
   easements shown on the final map shall reflect the composite plan as coordinated.

   Backflow prevention, meter sizing, and cross-connection control shall comply with the requirements of the
   Las Vegas Valley Water District and the Southern Nevada Health District.


E. Landscape (Conditions 25 through 28)

   Landscape and irrigation plans shall be prepared by a landscape architect registered in the State of Nevada
   and shall comply with Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Site Landscape and Screening Standards) of the Clark
   County Code, including the street frontage tree standard, plant palette, and turf restrictions in effect at the
   time of submittal.
     Streetscapes and medians shall be planted with low-water, climate-adapted plant material in accordance
    with the Southern Nevada Water Authority regional plant list. Turf shall not be installed within any
    streetscape, median, or right-of-way, nor within ten (10) feet of any street or curb.

    Landscape plans for any phase proposing turf shall comply with all applicable Title 30 turf-placement
    standards in effect at the time of the landscape submittal. Documentation supporting compliance shall
    accompany the landscape submittal.

    An irrigation demand worksheet shall be submitted with the landscape plans, showing water application
    rates by irrigation method, area by hydrozone, and total annual demand. The worksheet shall be updated to
    reflect any revision to the planting palette prior to landscape approval.


F. Other Reviewing Agencies (Conditions 29 through 31)

    Southern Nevada Health District: Approval of the sanitary sewer connection to the regional system, and of
    any private on-site treatment, shall be obtained prior to combustible construction. The Health District's
    certificate shall appear on the recorded final map.

    Clark County Recorder / Clark County Surveyor: The final map shall be prepared in accordance with NRS
    278.010 through 278.630 and the map checklist of the Clark County Surveyor. The Recorder's note required
    by NRS 278.5695 (examination of subsequent changes by reference to the cumulative index) shall appear on Sheet 1.

    Nevada Division of Water Resources: The Division's approval shall appear on the final map for each phase.



                            Statutory Presentation Deadlines (Reminder)

As stated above under Statutory Presentation Requirements, the first final map in the series must be presented
within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative map, and each
successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the date on which the
immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map terminates all proceedings
relating to the subdivision. An extension of not more than two (2) years may be granted only upon written
application filed after the applicable period has expired. The applicant is directed to compute its own
presentation deadlines from the operative events identified in NRS 278.360.


                                              Notice of Appeal

Any person aggrieved by this decision may appeal to the Clark County Board of County Commissioners by filing
a written notice of appeal with the Department of Comprehensive Planning within ten (10) calendar days of the
date of this letter. Appeals must be accompanied by the applicable fee. If no appeal is filed within the ten-day
period, this decision becomes final.


                                            Department Contact

Questions regarding these conditions of approval, or requests for interpretation, should be directed to:

Odette Marchetti Principal Planner Clark County Department of Comprehensive Planning 500 South Grand
Central   Parkway,    1st   Floor   Las    Vegas,   NV    89155   Direct:  (702)    555-4155   Email:
odette.marchetti@clarkcountynv.gov
 Sincerely,

(signed)

Odette Marchetti Principal Planner Clark County Department of Comprehensive Planning

Comprehensive Planning is in receipt of the written application submitted by Callaway Land Partners on
October 28, 2024, requesting an Extension of Time in which to present the first final map in the series under
TM-22-500041. This letter is the Department's response and, together with your application, constitutes the
official record for the tentative map file with respect to the extension question and the subsequent map clock.
                                   1. Governing statute — NRS 278.360

The extension mechanism available under Nevada law is set forth in NRS 278.360. In pertinent part, the statute
provides:

       "The governing body may, upon written application filed after the applicable period has expired,
       grant an extension of not more than two (2) years. An extension shall not be granted before the
       applicable presentation period has expired."

The statute is written in mandatory terms and its two operative preconditions — a written application, and a filing
date after the applicable period has expired — are jurisdictional. The County has no discretion to relax them.


                              2. Disposition of the 10/28/2024 application

Because the Callaway Land Partners application of 10/28/2024 was filed before the applicable presentation
period had expired, the County is without authority to act on it on the merits. The application is not properly
before the County until the applicable period has expired, and the County therefore declines to act on the
request in advance of the presentation period. This is a jurisdictional disposition, not a rejection on the merits.

Nothing in this letter forecloses any future written application filed by Callaway Land Partners in compliance with
the statutory precondition, if and when the applicable period has expired and Callaway has cause to seek relief.
Any such future application would be evaluated on its own record and on the standards then applicable.


                          3. Presentation of the first final map in the series

The Department has been advised, and the Clark County Recorder's index confirms, that the first final map in
the series under TM-22-500041 — Desert Sage Ranch Phases 1 & 2 (100 residential lots on approximately 100
acres, together with a remainder parcel for future Phase 3) — has been presented and recorded of record. The
applicant may consult the Recorder's public index for the recording particulars.

The four-year first-map presentation clock that runs from the date of tentative map approval has accordingly
been satisfied and is no longer at issue with respect to Desert Sage Ranch.


                           4. Presentation clock for successive final maps

The applicable statutory framework under NRS 278.360 continues to govern the tentative map. The applicant
and its design consultants are directed to confirm the operative presentation deadline for any successive map
with Comprehensive Planning. Failure to timely present a successive map within the applicable statutory period
would terminate all further proceedings under TM-22-500041.

 Submitting an Application for TAB Recommendation
 Any application requiring a recommendation of the Enterprise Town Advisory Board — including variance

 over all land use applications within their respective jurisdictions. The record of the TAB meeting — including any

    All work shall conform to Clark County Code Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Landscaping, Walls and Buffers), the
    Southern Nevada Regional Plant List, and the Clark County Standard Drawings current at the date of
    approval.
    Turf placement complies with Clark County Code sec. 30.64.030(j), which permits turf in conjunction with
    cemeteries, parks and schools and prohibits turf within ten feet of a street or curb. Restrictions of sec.
    30.64.030(j) may not be waived or varied and have been observed throughout.

    conjunction with the playground amenities called out on Sheet L-3 (slides, swings, and climbing structures),

    definitions.
    Streetscape planting is limited to drip-irrigated, desert-adapted species listed on the Southern Nevada
    Regional Plant List.
    All planted areas shall be irrigated by an automatic controller with rain-sensor lockout. Turf areas shall be
    spray-irrigated on a dedicated station; all other planted areas shall be drip-irrigated on separate stations.
    Street tree spacing shall meet the Clark County canopy standard of one tree per twenty linear feet of street
    frontage, measured continuously along each dedicated right-of-way.
    Minimum tree size at installation: 24-inch box, single-trunk, with a minimum caliper of 1.5 inches measured
    six inches above finish grade.
    All planting pits shall be excavated to twice the width and one-and-one-half times the depth of the root ball.

    outside the play area. Wood or bark mulches are not permitted.

    maintenance boundaries will be established by the declaration of covenants and are not repeated on these

 PREFACE
 The Uniform Unit Cost Schedule is published by Clark County Public Works for use by engineers of record, developers,
 and sureties in preparing an engineer's estimate of probable cost for subdivision improvements offered for bonding under
 Clark County Code Title 30 and the Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction Off-Site
 Improvements (Clark County Area).
 Unit prices set forth in this schedule reflect current Southern Nevada construction market conditions as surveyed by the
 Department across the twelve-month period preceding the effective date, drawing on bid tabulations for publicly bid
 subdivision and off-site improvement work in unincorporated Clark County and the incorporated municipalities of the Las
 Vegas Valley. The schedule is intended to normalize bonding across projects and to remove unit price disputes from the
 plan check cycle.
 Engineer's estimates for subdivision performance and labor-and-material bonds submitted to Clark County shall use the
 unit prices published in this schedule unless project-specific pricing is documented in writing (three qualified
 subcontractor quotes or an executed prime contract, dated within ninety (90) days of estimate submittal) and approved by
 Clark County Development Review prior to bond posting. Where project-specific pricing is approved, the higher of the
 two unit prices shall govern for bonding purposes.
 Contingency, mobilization, and design/inspection allowances stated in Section 11 shall be applied to the sum of itemized
 construction cost in every engineer's estimate submitted for bonding.

 ESCALATION AND REVIEW
 This schedule is reviewed annually by the Department. Revised schedules are issued each January, with an effective date
 of 01/01 of the calendar year. Between annual issues, the Department may issue a mid-year addendum where documented
 market conditions materially depart (±10 percent or greater on any category) from the published unit price. Bonding
 accepted against a superseded schedule remains in force at the amount posted; renewals, reissues, and increases occurring
 after a schedule effective date shall use the current schedule.
 Estimates submitted within thirty (30) days after a schedule effective date may, at the applicant's election, be computed
 against the immediately superseded schedule.

 SECTION 11 — CONTINGENCY, MOBILIZATION, AND ALLOWANCES
 The engineer's estimate for bonding shall include the following allowances, calculated as a percentage of the sum of items

  Where a subdivider requests reduction and release of bonded amount upon acceptance of an identifiable subset of
 improvements (e.g., off-site improvements accepted in advance of on-site completion), reductions shall be computed
 against the itemized construction subtotal only; mobilization, design/inspection, contingency, and escalation reserve shall
 remain proportional to remaining unfinished construction until final acceptance.

 SECTION 12 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
 12.01 Use of this Schedule. Unit prices published herein represent Southern Nevada market averages and are intended for
 bonding purposes only. They do not constitute a bid, a fixed-price contract, or an offer to construct. Contractors,
 subcontractors, and suppliers may propose actual pricing at variance with this schedule; such pricing does not modify the
 bonding amount unless approved in writing under the preface conditions.
 12.02 Rounding. Engineer's estimates prepared against this schedule shall carry unit prices to the cent as published and
 total costs to the dollar. The final bonded amount shall be rounded up to the next $1,000.
 12.03 Substitutions. Where an itemized quantity is bonded against a Uniform Standard Drawing that is superseded during
 the bond term, the substituted standard shall govern construction; the bonded unit price shall not be adjusted absent a
 formal amendment.
 12.04 Alternate Unit Prices. Alternate unit prices for materials or methods not appearing in this schedule shall be
 documented under the preface conditions and, once accepted, added to the estimate under the appropriate section with an
 "A" suffix (for example, 3.01A).
 12.05 Addenda. Addenda to this schedule are published on the Department's website and take effect on the date stated in
 the addendum. Applicants are responsible for verifying that the schedule referenced by the engineer's estimate is current at
 the time of submittal.
 12.06 Questions. Questions regarding the Uniform Unit Cost Schedule may be directed to Clark County Public Works,
 Development Review Division, at the address and telephone number stated above.

RECORDING REQUESTED BY AND WHEN RECORDED RETURN TO:

Vogel & Marsh LLP Attn: Adrienne Vogel, Esq. (NV Bar #10412) 3960 Howard Hughes Parkway, Suite 900 Las
Vegas, NV 89169

APN(s): 177-27-201-001 and consecutively assigned lot and parcel numbers within the recorded plat of Desert
Sage Ranch.

Recorded: December 23, 2024 Instrument No. 20241223-0004422 Book 175, Page 61, Official Records, Clark
County, Nevada

(Space above this line reserved for Recorder's use)


 DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS
                                 FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH

                          WITH COMMON AREA MAINTENANCE EXHIBIT

THIS DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH
(this "Declaration") is made and executed this 23rd day of December, 2024, by CALLAWAY LAND PARTNERS,
a Nevada limited liability company, having a principal place of business at 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400, Las
Vegas, NV 89148 (the "Declarant"), with reference to the facts recited below.



                                          ARTICLE I. RECITALS

A. Declarant is the owner in fee simple of certain real property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark
County, Nevada, being a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County,
Nevada, consisting of approximately 140.0 acres and commonly known and identified as the Desert Sage
Ranch subdivision (the "Property").

B. Declarant has caused the Property to be subdivided into three (3) sequential phases, being Phase 1, Phase
2, and Phase 3, together comprising residential lots, common-area parcels, streetscape parcels, and dedicated
public rights-of-way, all as more particularly depicted on the recorded final map(s) of the Property.

C. Concurrently with the execution and recordation of this Declaration, the First Final Map for Desert Sage
Ranch, Phases 1 and 2, being Map No. NFM-24-0118, is being recorded in the Office of the Clark County
Recorder at Book 175, Page 60 of Official Records ("First Final Map"). This Declaration is intended to be
recorded contemporaneously with, and to encumber the property depicted upon, the First Final Map, and to run
with and encumber the entire Property, including the Phase 3 remainder to be depicted on a successive final
map, upon its recordation.

D. It is the intention of Declarant to establish and impose upon the Property a general plan for the improvement,
protection, maintenance, and administration of Desert Sage Ranch as a planned residential community,
including without limitation the ownership and maintenance of certain common areas by a community
association formed for that purpose.
 E. Declarant intends that the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, assessments, charges, and liens
set forth below shall run with the land and be binding upon all persons or entities having or acquiring any right,
title, or interest in the Property or any portion thereof, and shall inure to the benefit of each Owner thereof.

F. Declarant has caused this Declaration to be prepared by Adrienne Vogel, Esq., of Vogel & Marsh LLP,
outside counsel to Declarant, in the manner set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, Declarant hereby declares that the Property shall be held, sold, conveyed, encumbered,
hypothecated, leased, used, occupied, and improved subject to the following covenants, conditions, restrictions,
easements, assessments, charges, and liens, all of which are declared to be in furtherance of a general plan
and scheme for the subdivision, improvement, and sale of the Property.

.....

Section 2.15. "Owner." The record holder of fee simple title to a Lot, excluding any person or entity holding title
solely as security for the performance of an obligation.

Section 2.16. "Property." All of the real property described in Article III below and shown upon the Map(s),
together with all Improvements thereon, and any additional property annexed hereto in accordance with this
Declaration.

Section 2.17. "Streetscape Common Area." Those parcels or strips of Common Area situated between the
back-of-curb of a public street and the front or side lot lines of the adjoining Lots (or, where applicable, between
the back-of-curb and a perimeter community wall), extending along all frontage of the Property, and improved
with sidewalks (where the sidewalk is not within the dedicated public right-of-way), desert planting, street trees,
and drip irrigation. Each Streetscape Common Area parcel is owned by the Association and is not part of any
Lot.



                                ARTICLE III. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION

Section 3.1. Legal Description of the Property. The Property subject to this Declaration is that certain real
property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark County, State of Nevada, more particularly described as
follows:

       A portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County, Nevada,
       containing approximately 140.0 acres, together with all easements, tenements, hereditaments, and
       appurtenances thereunto belonging, commonly known as Desert Sage Ranch, situated at the
       intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las Vegas, Nevada 89178.
 Section 3.2. Phasing. The Property is subject to development in three sequential phases:

(a) Phase 1 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area, and dedicated street
rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

(b) Phase 2 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area (including the Common-Area
Park designated Parcel A, the shared Detention Facility designated Parcel B, and the Entry Feature designated
Parcel C), and dedicated street rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

(c) Phase 3 — that portion of the Property consisting of approximately 40.0 acres, presently identified by Clark
County Assessor's Parcel Number 177-27-201-001, to be subdivided into approximately sixty (60) half-acre
residential Lots, together with associated streetscape Common Area and dedicated street rights-of-way, all to be
depicted upon a successive final map to be recorded by Declarant. Upon recordation of the Phase 3 final map,
the Lots and Common Area created thereby shall automatically be and become subject to this Declaration
without the necessity of any further instrument.

Section 3.3. Annexation of Successive Phases. Declarant reserves the right, exercisable in its sole discretion
and without the consent of any Owner, Mortgagee, or the Association, to annex Phase 3 (and any lawful
reconfiguration thereof) to the regime of this Declaration by recordation of a Supplemental Declaration in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder that (i) identifies the annexed property by reference to the recorded final
map, and (ii) states that the annexed property is thereby made subject to this Declaration.

Section 3.4. Public Rights-of-Way. All streets, alleys, and other public rights-of-way depicted upon any Map
are conveyed by dedication to Clark County or the applicable public body. No such dedicated area is Common
Area, and the Association bears no maintenance obligation for improvements accepted for public maintenance
within any such dedicated area, except as provided by written agreement with the applicable public body.



                                     ARTICLE IV. COMMON AREAS

Section 4.1. Establishment of Common Area. Declarant hereby establishes and dedicates for the common
use and enjoyment of the Owners, and conveys to the Association concurrently herewith and by the recordation
of each applicable Map, all Common Area, in fee simple, free and clear of all monetary encumbrances other
than the lien of current taxes and assessments not yet delinquent and matters of record specifically noted upon
the Map.

Section 4.2. Parcel A — Common-Area Park. The parcel designated Parcel A on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Common-Area Park. Parcel A is owned in fee simple
by the Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel A is improved by Declarant with landscaping, irrigation, and,
as installed by Declarant, any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed by Declarant, may
consist of slides, swings, and climbing structures). All landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting,
hardscape, and playground amenities installed upon Parcel A, as and where installed, constitute Common Area
Improvements owned by the Association.

Section 4.3. Parcel C — Entry Feature. The parcel designated Parcel C on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Entry Feature. Parcel C is owned in fee simple by the
Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel C is improved by Declarant with community entry monumentation,
community identification signage, decorative perimeter walls, drip-irrigated desert planting, and accent lighting.
All Improvements installed upon Parcel C constitute Common Area Improvements owned by the Association.
 Section 4.4. Streetscape Common Area. The streetscape strips depicted on each recorded Map along all
frontage of the Property, being situated between the back-of-curb of the adjoining public street and the front or
side lot lines of the abutting Lots (or the adjoining perimeter wall, where applicable), are hereby established as
Streetscape Common Area. Each such strip is owned in fee simple by the Association, is not part of any Lot,
and is improved by Declarant with street trees, drip-irrigated desert planting, decorative rock cover, and, where
applicable, community perimeter wall and sidewalk. The Streetscape Common Area extends continuously along
the entire street frontage of the Property, in the extent depicted upon the First Final Map and upon any
successive final map recorded for Phase 3.

Section 4.5. Distinct from Lots. The Common-Area Park (Parcel A), the shared Detention Facility (Parcel B),
the Entry Feature (Parcel C), and each Streetscape Common Area parcel are each Common Area owned and
maintained by the Association, and no such parcel is a Lot or any part of a Lot. No Owner has any right, by
virtue of ownership of a Lot, to construct, remove, alter, replace, or reconfigure any Improvement located within
any Common Area.

Section 4.6. Easements Appurtenant. Every Owner shall have a nonexclusive easement of use and
enjoyment in and to the Common Area, appurtenant to and passing with title to such Owner's Lot, subject to the
terms of this Declaration and the rules and regulations of the Association.

Section 4.7. Reserved Easements. Declarant reserves to itself, the Association, the Managing Agent, and their
respective employees, agents, and contractors, a perpetual easement over, upon, across, and through each
Common Area parcel for the purposes of installing, inspecting, maintaining, repairing, and replacing Common
Area Improvements, including without limitation landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting, and
playground amenities, as installed.

Section 4.8. No Partition. The Common Area shall remain undivided. No Owner or other person shall bring any
action for the partition or division of the Common Area, and each Owner waives any right of partition such
Owner may hold at law or in equity.



                         ARTICLE V. MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT

Section 5.1. Association Responsibility. The Association shall be responsible for the continuous and ongoing
maintenance, repair, and replacement of the Common Area and all Improvements located thereon, including
without limitation:

(a) all landscaping within the Common Area, including all turf, planting, groundcover, shrubs, and trees, as and
where installed;

(b) all irrigation infrastructure within the Common Area, including without limitation mainline, laterals, valves,
valve boxes, backflow prevention assemblies, controllers, wiring, and emitters;

(c) all playground amenities located within the Common Area, as installed, including without limitation slides,
swings, climbing structures, and any associated resilient surfacing, safety zone materials, and containment
curbing;

(d) all hardscape within the Common Area, including sidewalks (where not within a dedicated public right-of-way
accepted for public maintenance), walls, monumentation, signage, benches, and accent lighting; and

(e) all other Improvements installed within the Common Area from time to time by Declarant or the Association.
 Section 5.2. Delegation to Managing Agent. The Association hereby delegates the day-to-day performance of
the maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations set forth in Section 5.1 to its Managing Agent, being, as of
the date of this Declaration, Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company
having offices at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120. The Managing Agent shall perform
such obligations pursuant to and in accordance with the written management agreement entered into between
the Association and the Managing Agent (the "Management Agreement"), which Management Agreement may

 2.2 Land Use and Development Program

Phase 3 consists of 60 single-family detached residential lots of nominal half-acre size (typical lot 100 ft ×
220 ft, typical lot area 22,000 sf). The subdivision layout is an internal loop street configuration providing
public-street frontage to all 60 lots, together with two HOA-owned common-area parcels (Parcel D — park;
Parcel E — detention basin). The land use is exclusively single-family residential; the plan set contains no
commercial, mixed-use, school, or institutional component.



2.3 Site Access

Site access is provided by a single permanent full-movement connection between the Phase 3 internal street
system and the surrounding public roadway network:

    • Desert Sage Parkway at Windmill Lane — new full-movement intersection at the south boundary of the
    Phase 3 parcel, at proposed Station 22+80 on Windmill Lane. Desert Sage Parkway is the north-south spine
    street of the Phase 3 subdivision (60-ft public right-of-way, 36-ft back-to-back curb-and-gutter, 5-ft detached
    sidewalk each side) and terminates at Windmill Lane at the site's south boundary. Return radii are Type C,
    30 ft, per Clark County Uniform Standard Drawing No. 201.

The Phase 3 interior street network additionally comprises Sage Bloom Drive, Rattlesnake Loop, Chuckwalla
Way, Ocotillo Court, Yucca Court (cul-de-sac stub) and Cholla Court (cul-de-sac terminus), all proposed for
dedication to Clark County for public use under Final Map FM-26-100290.

map:

5.7 Traffic Control at the Intersection
 Consistent with the LOS results above and the applicable Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)
signal warrants, no traffic signal is warranted at Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill Lane at Phase 3 buildout.
STOP-controlled operation on the Desert Sage Parkway (southbound) approach is appropriate. Standard R1-1
STOP signage, associated street-name signs (D3-1), and an advance intersection warning sign on Windmill
Lane if sight-distance verification identifies any restriction, are recommended.

Intersection sight distance (ISD) at Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill Lane was reviewed against the AASHTO
Green Book sight-distance criteria for a 35-mph major-road design speed. Available sight distance in both
directions along Windmill Lane exceeds the calculated minimum ISD for both left- and right-turn maneuvers from
the stopped southbound approach; no clear-sight-triangle grading modification is required.



5.8 Summary

At buildout of Phase 3, the Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill Lane intersection is projected to operate at LOS A
overall and LOS B on the worst (stop-controlled) approach during both the AM and PM peak hours. Delay
increases attributable to the project are negligible and well within normal variability of a residential T-intersection
of this configuration.



                                    6. ACCESS SPACING STANDARDS


6.1 Applicable Standards

Access management on the surrounding collector roadway network is governed by the Clark County Uniform
Standard Drawings and Clark County Development Code Title 30 access management provisions applicable to
collector roadways. The applicable spacing standards include:

    • Minimum access spacing on collector roadway — spacing between adjacent full-movement public
    street intersections along a collector shall be consistent with the collector-classification spacing table in the
    applicable Clark County / RTC Uniform Standards. For collector roads of the classification of Windmill Lane,
    the minimum full-movement intersection spacing standard is on the order of 300–600 feet, depending on
    posted speed and adjacent land use.

    • Corner clearance — full-movement site access on a collector shall be offset from the nearest upstream
    and downstream intersection consistent with the applicable corner-clearance standard.

    • Return geometry — return curb radii shall conform to Clark County Uniform Standard Drawing No. 201
    (Type C returns at collector / local street intersection), which are the returns provided at the Desert Sage
    Parkway / Windmill Lane connection.


6.2 Review of the Proposed Connection

The single permanent connection between Phase 3 and the surrounding roadway network is at the proposed
intersection of Desert Sage Parkway with Windmill Lane at the south boundary of the parcel. This connection
has been reviewed against the applicable Clark County collector-street access spacing standard:

    • Nearest upstream collector intersection to the west (Rainbow Boulevard / Windmill Lane) — located
    approximately 1,320 ft west of the proposed Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill Lane intersection.
     • Nearest downstream collector or local street intersection to the east — approximately 900 ft east of
    the proposed Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill Lane intersection.

The proposed single permanent connection is spaced consistent with the applicable collector-road
access spacing standard, with intersection offsets well in excess of the minimum spacing threshold for a
collector of the classification of Windmill Lane. The proposed return geometry is per Clark County Uniform
Standard Drawing No. 201. Corner clearance is met.

No conflict with Clark County access management standards has been identified at the proposed connection.



6.3 Coordination with Improvement Plans

The Phase 3 street and access geometry reviewed here is consistent with the Phase 3 improvement plan set
(Sheets C-1 through C-9, prepared by Sundial Engineering & Survey) and with Sheet FA-1 (Street and Fire
Access Plan). The single permanent connection at Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill Lane is the connection
shown on the current plan set between the Phase 3 internal loop street system and the surrounding roadway
network.

Based on the analysis presented in this Traffic Impact Statement, Dune Traffic Engineering LLC offers the
following recommendations to Callaway Land Partners and Sundial Engineering & Survey in connection with

    Site access geometry as shown may be constructed. The proposed Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill
    Lane intersection is spaced consistent with Clark County access management standards for a collector

    Traffic control. Provide standard STOP control (MUTCD R1-1) on the Desert Sage Parkway southbound
    approach at Windmill Lane, together with corresponding STOP-line pavement marking, street-name
    signage (D3-1), and standard curb-return geometry per Clark County Uniform Standard Drawing No. 201.
    No traffic signal is warranted.

    Auxiliary turn lanes. No auxiliary left-turn or right-turn lanes are warranted on Windmill Lane at the Desert
    Sage Parkway intersection at Phase 3 buildout. No offsite widening of Windmill Lane is triggered by Phase
    3.

    Sight distance. Provide and maintain the sight-distance triangle at the Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill

    Signing and striping. Coordinate the final signing and striping plan for the Windmill Lane / Desert Sage

    Construction traffic. During construction of Phase 3, provide a Temporary Traffic Control Plan for

    applicable permit.

   Compliance Bulletin and Functional Turf Definitions

  Bulletin No.           WRC-2024-07                                  Issue Date                    Q4 2024

   1. Purpose
   This bulletin implements the nonfunctional turf prohibition enacted by the Nevada Legislature in Assembly Bill
   356 (2021) and administered within the SNWA service area by the Southern Nevada Water Authority in
   cooperation with its member agencies. Assembly Bill 356 directs the removal of nonfunctional turf from
   properties served by the Colorado River Commission of Nevada and, by extension, from properties served by
   SNWA member agencies.
   The compliance deadline for the removal or conversion of all nonfunctional turf on properties subject to the
   prohibition is 12/31/2026. On and after that date, the presence of nonfunctional turf on a property subject to the
   prohibition constitutes a continuing violation of the state statute and of the water service rules of the SNWA
   member agencies.
   The prohibition applies to, without limitation:

   •   Homeowner association (HOA) owned or managed common-area property, including entry features,
       streetscape strips, medians, park parcels, tot lots, and greenbelts;

   •   Commercial, industrial, mixed-use, institutional, and multi-family residential properties;

   •   Governmental, quasi-governmental, and school-district properties;
   •   Vacant parcels held for future development on which existing turf remains irrigated.
   Property owners and their agents are directed to identify all turf areas on affected properties, to classify each
   area as functional or nonfunctional under the definitions set out in Section 3, and to schedule conversion of
   nonfunctional areas so that removal is complete on or before the deadline.

   2. Single-Family Residential Carve-Out
   The nonfunctional turf prohibition does not apply to turf located within an individually-owned single-family
   residential lot. Turf inside the recorded boundary of a single-family residential lot — front yard, side yard, back
   yard, and any other area within the four corners of the lot as recorded — is exempt from the mandate
   established by AB 356 and this bulletin. Owners of single-family residential lots remain subject to the general
   water-waste ordinances and outdoor-watering restrictions of their retail purveyor but are not required by AB
   356 to remove existing turf.
   The single-family residential carve-out is lot-based, not project-based. The following areas are outside the
   carve-out and remain fully subject to the prohibition even where they lie within a subdivision the zoning of

   •   HOA-owned or HOA-managed common-area parcels of any description, including but not limited to park

   •   Streetscape and parkway areas between the back of curb and the right-of-way line, or between the

   •   Any parcel held in common ownership by two or more lot owners through a homeowner association or
